questions.question_text: Find the average rate of change of $f(x) = 3x^2 - 2$ over the interval $[1, 4]$.

options.why: Calculates the difference in function values without dividing by the interval width ($46 - 1 = 45$).
Divides $f(4)$ by the upper endpoint $4$ ($46 \div 4 = 11.5$) instead of computing $\frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}$.
Evaluates the average rate of the linear term $3x$ rather than the quadratic $3x^2$.
Calculates the rise $21 - 5 = 16$ but forgets to divide by the run $6 - 2 = 4$.
Inverts the gradient formula by computing run over rise ($\frac{4}{16} = 0.25$).
Averages the coordinates of the endpoints $\frac{2+5}{2} = 3.5$ instead of finding gradient.

questions.question_text: A culture of cells grows such that its mass is $20\text{ mg}$ at $t = 2\text{ hours}$ and $80\text{ mg}$ at $t = 7\text{ hours}$. What is the average growth rate of the culture over this time?

options.why: Calculates the total mass change $80 - 20 = 60\text{ mg}$ without dividing by the elapsed time of $5\text{ hours}$.
Divides final mass $80$ by the final time $7$ rather than calculating rate over the interval.
Divides initial mass $20$ by $2\text{ hours}$ ($20 \div 2 = 10\text{ mg/h}$) instead of finding average rate over $[2, 7]$.

questions.question_text:
The table lists values for a non-linear function $g(x)$:
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} x & 1 & 3 & 5 & 7 \\ \hline g(x) & 4 & 10 & 22 & 40 \end{array}$
Which interval has the highest average rate of change?

options.why: Rate over $[1, 3]$ is $\frac{10 - 4}{2} = 3$, which is the lowest rate among the intervals.
Rate over $[3, 5]$ is $\frac{22 - 10}{2} = 6$, which is lower than the rate over $[5, 7]$ of $9$.
Overall rate over $[1, 7]$ is $\frac{40 - 4}{6} = 6$, which is not greater than the subinterval $[5, 7]$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Rate over }[1, 3] = \dfrac{10 - 4}{3 - 1} = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3$
$\text{Rate over }[3, 5] = \dfrac{22 - 10}{5 - 3} = \dfrac{12}{2} = 6$
$\text{Rate over }[5, 7] = \dfrac{40 - 22}{7 - 5} = \dfrac{18}{2} = 9$
$\text{The interval }[5, 7]\text{ has the highest average rate of change } (9 > 6 > 3).$

questions.question_text: Calculate the average rate of change of $f(x) = x^3 - 2x$ over the interval $[0, 3]$.

options.why: Calculates the total change in function values $21 - 0 = 21$ without dividing by the interval width $3$.
Evaluates only the $x^3$ term ($27 \div 3 = 9$) and adds $0.5$ incorrectly.
Mistakenly assumes the average rate equals the upper endpoint value $x = 3$.
Calculates the total vertical drop $5 - 45 = -40\text{ m}$ but omits dividing by $\Delta t = 2\text{ s}$.
Omits the negative sign, ignoring that height is decreasing as the object falls.
Divides change in height by total time $4$ instead of interval time $3 - 1 = 2\text{ s}$.

questions.question_text: During a dry spell, the water level in a reservoir drops from $34\text{ m}$ to $18\text{ m}$ over a span of $8\text{ days}$. What is the average rate of change in the water level?

options.why: Gives the total change in water level $18 - 34 = -16\text{ m}$ without dividing by $8\text{ days}$.
Gives a positive rate of change even though the water level is decreasing.
Divides initial depth $18$ by $8\text{ days}$ ($18 \div 8 = 2.25$) rather than computing $\frac{\Delta h}{\Delta t}$.

questions.question_text: Find the average rate of change of $f(x) = 2x^2 + 3x$ over the interval $[2, 2+h]$ in terms of $h$.

options.why: Evaluates $f(h)$ instead of computing the secant difference quotient $\frac{f(2+h)-f(2)}{h}$.
Differentiates with respect to $h$ incorrectly rather than simplifying the algebraic quotient.
Expands $(2+h)^2$ as $4 + 2h + h^2$, omitting the factor of $2$ on the cross-term.
